official.deadline_note: The 2027 round opened on 14 July 2026 and closed on 9 September 2026 at 3:00pm UK time, with interviews for shortlisted applicants between 13 and 29 April 2027 and results expected in July 2027. The scheme page lists the decision date as 31 May 2027. No dates have been published for the following round.
official.application_cycle: 2027 round (fellowships expected to commence between 1 October 2027 and 1 January 2028)
official.status_note: The University Research Fellowship scheme page lists Status: Closed for the 2027 round, with open date 14 July 2026 and close date 09 September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition fee is charged to the fellow; the award is a salary-and-research-costs fellowship. Funding may include a contribution to a four-year PhD studentship including PhD stipend and fees.
benefits: Eight years of independent research funding, with years six to eight subject to satisfactory progress demonstrated in a mid-fellowship review at the start of year four

Research Fellow's basic salary costs and associated on-costs at 100% contribution, including PRSI and employer pension, budgeted on the Research Ireland Team Member scales (Research Fellow scale Level 3 Points 1-4 in years 1-5, Senior Research Fellow scale Level 4 Points 1-3 in years 6-8)
Overhead costs equivalent to 30% of the value of the award excluding equipment
Research expenses up to EUR 720,000 over eight years, with a maximum of EUR 90,000 per annum expected and underspend carried over
Equipment at 100% contribution, with items over EUR 25,000 requiring additional justification
Public engagement funding of up to EUR 8,000 over the duration of the fellowship
Contribution to a four-year PhD studentship including PhD stipend and fees, and contributions to research assistance and other staff costs including PDRAs and technical support
Relocation expenses and visa costs for the applicant and dependants (partner and children)

Flexibility to hold the fellowship full-time or part-time for health reasons or caring responsibilities, with provision for maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave and financial support for childcare costs arising from attending conferences
Access to Royal Society career development and engagement opportunities
eligibility: Early career, postdoctoral researchers of any nationality with between three to eight years of actual research experience since their PhD by the closing date of the round; career breaks are taken into consideration

Cases of exceptional talent can be considered case by case for applicants with less than three years of research experience, requiring a letter of support from the Head of Department that must be submitted and flagged to the Grants team before the application itself
Research must be within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, including but not limited to biological research, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics

The fellowship must be hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body situated in the Republic of Ireland; eligible bodies include universities, technological universities, institutes of technology and independent not-for-profit public research organisations receiving a significant share of their total funding from public sources
Applicants of any nationality may apply, and those requiring a visa are eligible for the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement
requirements: The scheme is not for postdoctoral researchers who already lead a research group, or who are named as lead applicant (Principal Investigator) on an external award
The scheme is not for academic staff with a tenure track faculty position or permanent academic post (including proleptic position) in a university or not-for-profit research organisation

The scheme is not for Independent Research Fellows who currently hold, or have previously held, a nationally competitive research fellowship equivalent to a URF, defined as one awarded through a national open competition, of four or more years duration, portable to any host organisation, providing support for the award holder's salary and research costs or staff, and intended to enable the award holder to establish independence
The Society does not support clinical or interventional research on humans at the individual or group level, social sciences, or humanities

The Head of Department must provide a statement of support through Flexi-Grant confirming the host organisation's ability to comply with the Conditions of Award, and it must be completed before the closing of the round
A nominated referee must provide a confidential reference through Flexi-Grant before the closing of the round
Applicants must remain eligible until the time of the application deadline
Resubmissions are allowed as long as the applicant continues to meet the eligibility criteria
documents: Research proposal and eight-year costed budget submitted through Flexi-Grant
Head of Department statement of support submitted through Flexi-Grant
Confidential reference from one nominated referee submitted through Flexi-Grant
Evidence of research experience since the award of the PhD
For applicants requesting PhD studentship costs, a statement from the applicant and Head of Department confirming the host organisation's underwriting and supervision commitments
For named collaborators, letters of support
selection_criteria: Applications pass eligibility checks, then are assessed by at least two members of the relevant Research Appointment Panel
A longlist is drawn up and longlisted proposals are subject to high quality independent peer review
Following peer review, proposals are reassessed by the assigned Panel members and a shortlist for interview is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chair
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society
Irish and UK candidates are assessed together through the normal Royal Society peer review process
coverage: Contribution to the award holder's salary, including PRSI and employer pension, at 100% contribution on the Research Ireland budgeting scale
Indirect and estate costs, equivalent to 30% of the value of the award excluding equipment
Equipment costs and research expenses including consumables and travel, up to EUR 720,000 over eight years
Contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs
Contribution to staff costs including PDRA, PhD studentships and technical support
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants
Public engagement activities up to EUR 8,000 over the duration of the fellowship
application_method: Apply through the Royal Society Flexi-Grant online application and grant management system; paper-based applications will not be accepted

Invite the Head of Department at the host organisation to provide a statement of support through the Participants tab, and invite one nominated referee to provide a confidential reference through Flexi-Grant
Ensure all contributions by the Head of Department, Nominated Referee and Research Office are completed before the closing of the round, as they are required for successful submission
For exceptional-talent cases, submit the Head of Department support letter separately to urf@royalsociety.org and flag it with the Grants team before the application itself
official.application_route: Secure a host within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body, then submit a costed eight-year proposal through Flexi-Grant with a Head of Department statement of support and a referee reference completed before the deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time, with provision for part-time working for health reasons or caring responsibilities
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants can be of any nationality. The fellowship must be hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body situated in the Republic of Ireland.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants of any nationality; those requiring a visa are eligible for the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must fall within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences - biological research, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics. Clinical or interventional research on humans at the individual or group level, social sciences and humanities are not supported. Applicants must be hosted at a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body in the Republic of Ireland.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal with a full eight-year costed budget is required. The proposal must demonstrate how the award will lead to scientific independence.
official.duration: 8 years, with years 6-8 subject to satisfactory progress and completion of a mid-fellowship review at the start of year four
official.description: The Royal Society and Taighde Eireann - Research Ireland have established a partnership to ensure that outstanding early career researchers from the Republic of Ireland have the opportunity to establish an independent research career, awarding a prestigious Royal Society - Research Ireland University Research Fellowship. Successful candidates are awarded a fellowship by the Royal Society, the cost of which is met by Research Ireland, and are expected to be strong candidates for permanent posts in universities at the end of their fellowships.
official.program_type: Eight-year independent research fellowship for early career scientists

english_requirement - no English language requirement is published for this scheme

verification.notes: Read the Royal Society University Research Fellowship page, the Republic of Ireland scheme notes in full (30 pages) and the application dates page. Confirmed the closed 2027 round with close date 9 September 2026, the eight-year duration with mid-fellowship review, the EUR 720,000 research-expenses cap and EUR 8,000 public-engagement cap, the 30% overhead rule, salary and PhD studentship provisions, relocation and visa cover, the Research Ireland Eligible Research Body host requirement and the 6.3% success rate for 2025/26. No total award maximum is published for the Ireland arm, so funding_amount is null.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship with a fixed value you can compare against others: you build an eight-year budget yourself, and the arithmetic that matters is that research expenses are capped at EUR 720,000 across the whole fellowship with roughly EUR 90,000 a year expected, against a salary contribution pegged to the Research Ireland Team Member scales and 30% overheads on top. The host requirement is structural rather than clerical - the fellowship must sit inside a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body in the Republic of Ireland - and the Head of Department statement plus your referee's reference must both be complete inside Flexi-Grant before the round closes, so a slow referee kills the application no matter how good the science is. Historical success rates of roughly 6 to 7% mean this is a long shot by design, and the in-person interview at the Royal Society in April is where the award is actually won or lost.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdoctoral natural scientists, three to eight years post-PhD, who do not yet lead a group or hold a permanent post and who have a credible Irish host department willing to underwrite the appointment.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your exact years of actual research experience against the 3-8 year window measured to the round's closing date, and gather evidence of any career breaks so they can be discounted
Confirm your intended host is on the Research Ireland list of eligible research bodies before approaching a department

Open the conversation with your Head of Department early, since their statement of support must be completed in Flexi-Grant before the round closes and exceptional-talent support letters must be emailed and flagged separately beforehand
Agree the referee's Flexi-Grant contribution well in advance and confirm which email address they will use, since a wrong address delays processing

Build the eight-year budget on the Research Ireland Team Member salary scales with single-point annual increments, and keep research expenses within the EUR 720,000 envelope while front-loading years 1-5
Separate equipment from the research-expenses line and pre-justify anything over EUR 25,000
common_rejection_risks: Already leading a research group or being named Principal Investigator on an external award, which makes you ineligible regardless of record
Holding a tenure-track faculty position or permanent academic post, including a proleptic position

Holding, or having held, a nationally competitive fellowship that is open-competition, four or more years, portable, covers salary and research costs or staff and is intended to establish independence
Proposing clinical or interventional research on humans, or anything in the social sciences or humanities, which the Society does not support
A Head of Department statement or referee reference left incomplete at the closing date, which prevents successful submission
Requesting more than EUR 90,000 of research costs in a year without a clear rationale for exceeding the annual expectation
Accepting a permanent post before the deadline, which must be declared and changes your eligibility position
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any equipment the Society negotiates down or declines to fund, salary above the Research Ireland budgeting scale unless the host organisation supplements it, relocation and visa costs for dependants beyond partner and children, and any costs not listed as eligible such as indirect items outside the 30% overhead rate.
document_audit: The Head of Department statement of support is visible to the applicant, so read it before submission and correct any mischaracterisation of your independence route
Referees and other participants must each hold a Flexi-Grant account; if your referee already has one, they must use that account rather than creating a duplicate

Requests for PhD studentship costs need an additional statement from you and your Head of Department confirming the host will underwrite the remaining cost and provide alternative supervision if you leave
For applicants requesting PhD studentship costs, an additional statement of support is required per the Programme Specific Funding Rules
alerts: The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 at 3:00pm UK time, so the next opportunity is the following cycle and no dates are published yet
Interviews for the 2027 round are in person at the Royal Society between 13 and 29 April 2027, and results are expected in July 2027 - there is a long gap between submission and decision
Career breaks are accounted for, and maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave attracts additional time on top of the leave taken
If you accept a permanent post or equivalent fellowship after the deadline you can stay in the competition, but if offered the URF you would be required to resign from that position
Resubmission is allowed, so an unsuccessful first attempt does not close the door
Adjustments for disabled applicants include a deadline extension, a different application format and support at interview; requests go to adjustments@royalsociety.org in confidence
Irish and UK candidates are assessed together through the same peer review, so do not expect a separate or easier Irish track
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Flexi-Grant application with the eight-year costed research proposal, secure the Head of Department statement of support and the nominated referee's reference inside Flexi-Grant before the closing date, then eligibility checks, Panel Review 1, independent peer review, Panel Review 2, shortlisting, and an in-person interview at the Royal Society.
